scope.objective: Review the complete candidate delta for Hyperliquid signer/grant binding, transport/origin/TLS, credential generation, mutation locking, provider acceptance boundaries, XML/subprocess hardening and JavaScript/TypeScript scanner changes.
scope.method: Direct source inspection, full delta enumeration, real Python 3.12/CCXT 4.5.75 boundary tests, official Node 22 suite, frontend suite, build/lint/typecheck and targeted static analysis. No provider request or live order was issued.

verifiedProperties.property: Hyperliquid signer is cryptographically derived and distinguished from the master wallet.
Agent credentials are restricted to Testnet with an exact two-field secret shape.
Grant role, signer row, uniqueness and minimum remaining validity are re-read from read-only Testnet Info responses.
Grant re-read, credential fingerprint and generation checks occur under the per-account mutation lock and before the mutation body.
Agent SDK routes are pinned to exact Testnet HTTPS/WSS origins, POST-only, query/fragment-free, proxy-free and REST-only for exchange actions.
Reviewed exchange action scope permits only order, cancel/cancelByCloid and cross updateLeverage with bounded first-DEX asset IDs; builder/vault/foreign action envelopes fail closed.
Live provider exposure remains default-deny in both Python and TypeScript until a pinned provenance implementation and independently pinned reviewer key exist.
Python and Node signed-grant canonicalization, account/product/time binding and descriptor-safe reads are cross-language tested.
Cobertura path verification uses a bounded linear parser, rejects DTD/entities/external resolution, and invokes only a fixed no-shell Git argv.
Drive mirroring hashes and uploads through the same opened file handle; remote verification still binds the expected digest and size.
B2 audit refactors preserve serialization, bounded body, disconnect, replay and verified-persistence semantics under 23 tests.

limitations: This is an offline local implementation review, not a completion or provider-acceptance decision.
No network request, credential loading, Testnet operation, live order, cancellation or cleanup was performed.
The full Python suite cannot be green until the six matrix references and the separate implementation receipt are renewed through their normal independent-review process.
One non-official frontend invocation produced a single transient operator-maintenance test failure; the isolated test and the complete official rerun passed, so no stable defect was demonstrated.
Semgrep community rule packs are supplemental and do not replace the repository lint, test, CI or external scanner gates.
